messages:
Lina (PM): quick follow-ups from today's all-hands — can leadership clarify a couple points on mission vs gtm? i.e., elevator pitch for sales, where we lean product vs infra, and the top 2 competitor threats we should watch for?
Jamie (CEO): sure — short answer: mission remains 'make high-performance reliable inference accessible to every engineering team.' for sales pitch: 'Redwood delivers predictable inference economics and the same dev experience from hosted to private, so you don’t trade velocity for compliance.' keep it under 20 words.
Ravi (Sales): that helps — when do we lead with Dedicated vs Hosted in pitch decks? any clear adoption trigger?
Jamie (CEO): recommend rule of thumb: lead with Hosted for PLG / proof-of-concept. If a prospect mentions SLAs, data residency, or >$X/mo committed spend, switch to Dedicated/private conversation. sales ops will get the specific dollar threshold next week. :+1:
Ana (CTO): to add — technically Dedicated/Private is not just capacity; it's where we expose guaranteed latency SLOs, customer-controlled networking, and encryption-in-use options. that'll be the checklist for the handoff from AE -> Solutions.
Ben (SRE): timeline check: when do we expect GA for Private (VPC/on-prem packaging)? customers are asking.
Ana (CTO): GA target Q3. current plan: limited private pilots in June, broader GA rollout and docs in August. there are two outstanding items: simplified onboarding for KMS integrations and an automated health-check agent.
Morgan (Research): on positioning vs cloud AI services — we should emphasize 'serving + observability' not just model access. our differentiator is predictable unit economics and rollouts with traceable quality regressions. that's what enterprise buyers care about.
Ravi (Sales): competitor question — how do we talk about proprietary model providers and 'we have your model' arguments? some prospects assume owning models is the moat.
Jamie (CEO): acknowledge model ownership but pivot: 'model ownership is only part of the stack; the real moat is how you serve it — latency, cost per token, reliability, and operational tooling.' use the analogy: model = engine, Redwood = transmission + dashboard + pit crew.
Ana (CTO): also call out our smart routing and fallback policies in the pitch: when top-tier capacity is constrained we can fall back to compatible variants automatically — this keeps product UX stable without manual intervention.
Lina (PM): got it. any guidance on messaging for benchmarks? folks ask for numbers.
Morgan (Research): share vetted benchmarks only. highlight 99th pct latency, tokens/sec, and cost per token for common seq lengths. don't cherry-pick single-case numbers.
EvalsBot: pinned -> internal benchmarking dashboard: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks (team-only)
Ravi (Sales): thanks — for objection handling: if a buyer says 'we'll just run this ourselves on cloud' — best short rebuttal?
Jamie (CEO): 'You could, but you'll spend months tuning kernels, optimizing batching, and building ops — we give you that in weeks plus production SLAs. also, unit economics differ once you factor in engineering time and tail latency.'
Ben (SRE): practical ops note: emphasize our caching and continuous batching story in tech calls. that’s usually the surprise win vs self-hosted.
Lina (PM): action items I heard: 1) sales ops deck blurb for Dedicated trigger, 2) updated one-sentence pitch, 3) publish GA timeline for Private, 4) vetted bench numbers to sales. can leadership confirm?
Jamie (CEO): confirm. i'll post final one-sentence pitch and a short FAQ tomorrow.
Ana (CTO): i'll post the GA timeline + tech checklist by EOD Friday.
Ravi (Sales): i'll update the pitch templates and objection handling doc after Jamie posts.
Morgan (Research): i'll curate a short benchmark summary (3 slides) focused on latency, throughput, and cost.
Lina (PM): perfect — thanks all. small follow-up: do we want a canned line for marketing assets that calls out 'unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, private'?
Jamie (CEO): yes — marketing can use: 'One API. Any deployment. Predictable inference economics.' leave room for localization.
Lina (PM): great, closing this thread — will pull actions into the roadmap. :white_check_mark:
